pricing_framing: Remove the unsupported "up to 60% off" claim from title, H1, and meta description. No original price is displayed (content gap #2, AI flag), and all competitor pricing data is for luxury spa packages ($380–$780), NOT B12/MIC injection services (research red flag: "competitor data is not product-comparable"). Without comparable pricing, the discount claim cannot be verified and erodes trust. Instead, frame as "$40.50 for [quantity] injections plus InBody analysis" — lead with what the customer gets, not an unverifiable saving. If merchant can provide a documented original price, display it; otherwise, position on value and experience rather than discount percentage.
executive_summary: The page scores 5.1/10 overall, with clarity at only 4/10. The #1 problem is that customers cannot tell what they're actually buying — "B12 and MIC Fat Burner injections" is ambiguous (one of each? multiple sessions?). The #2 issue is an unsupported "up to 60% off" claim with no original price shown and no comparable competitor pricing (all comps are spa packages, not injections). Fixing quantity clarity, removing the unverifiable discount claim, and explaining what MIC is could lift conversion 20–30%.
